topic: Valuation of Unsold Stock on Consignment
concept_topic: Valuation of Unsold Stock on Consignment
voice: teacher: af_heart, girl: af_sarah, boy: am_fenrir

script.title: Valuing unsold stock on consignment
script.caption_hook: Why does unsold consignment stock carry expenses too?

lines.say: Ma'am, why does unsold stock carry some expenses too?
Unsold goods still belong to the consignor, so he values them in his books.
So is the value just the cost?
Cost plus one-time expenses up to the godown: freight, insurance in transit, loading, unloading, octroi or entry tax.
What about godown rent and selling expenses?
Those come after the door. Till the door, not the floor! They go to Consignment account.
Consignee paid the unloading. Does that count?
Yes! Whoever paid, add them for the whole consignment. Then take only the unsold share.
How do we take that share?
Closing stock equals unsold units times cost plus expenses, divided by units sent.

board.title: Value of unsold stock
board.sub: U unsold, Q sent, C cost, E expenses to godown

lines.say: Sent 100 units costing ₹20,000. Expenses ₹3,000. Unsold 20 units. Stock is 20 by 100 of ₹23,000.
What if goods were sent at invoice price?
Take loaded invoice value plus expenses, then create Stock Reserve for the loading on unsold goods.
Remember: till the door, not the floor.

check_notes: Writer: Worked example: expenses ₹3,000 assumed to be non-recurring costs up to the godown (freight, insurance in transit, unloading); stock = 20/100 × 23,000 = ₹4,600. Octroi/entry tax mentioned as 'where levied' (legacy item after GST). Word count is near the upper limit.

Checker: Line 4 and its board ('Octroi or entry tax'): both taxes were folded into GST in 2017, so as current examples they are out of date. They still appear in older textbook problems. Correct version: say 'octroi or entry tax (older problems), or any other non-recurring charge up to the consignee's godown, such as carriage or cartage'.

Checker: Line 8 ('Whoever paid, add them for the whole consignment'): 'them' could be heard as all of the consignee's expenses. Correct version: 'Whoever paid, add the non-recurring expenses up to the godown, whether the consignor or the consignee paid them, for the whole consignment. Then take only the unsold share.' This makes clear that recurring expenses paid by the consignee, such as godown rent, are not added.

Checker: Line 10 voice ('unsold units times cost plus expenses, divided by units sent'): spoken aloud, the order of operations is unclear, and 'cost' could be taken as cost per unit. Correct version: 'unsold units divided by units sent, times total cost plus total expenses to the godown'. The board's 'C cost, E expenses' should also say 'total cost of goods sent' and 'total non-recurring expenses'.
